tool_args.rationale: The five observations span gradients only up to 2.44, close to the stated avalanche threshold range, so a high-gradient probe is the smallest relevant measurement to distinguish ordinary siphon saturation from threshold-driven collapse. The current rows cannot safely support fresh-confirmation accuracy at the requested tolerance if that branch is active.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit node P supercritical siphon avalanche now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All five observations are below the proposed threshold region; the avalanche term is unobserved and its threshold/strength are not identifiable.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit node C/D static siphon model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The observed monotone-concave response is compatible with a baseline siphon, but does not rule out an avalanche onset just beyond the sampled gradient range.
The observed signatures support a static concave response, not a coupled-memory ODE; trajectory data would be unnecessarily costly.
No identified ambiguity calls for this nuisance measurement.
